items.text: Jessica Ancona has served as mayor of El Monte since 2020 and on the City Council since 2018. She works as a high school assistant principal. Before joining the City Council, she served five years on the El Monte City School District Board.

sentences.text: Jessica Ancona has served as mayor of El Monte since 2020 and on the City Council since 2018.
She works as a high school assistant principal.
Before joining the City Council, she served five years on the El Monte City School District Board.

items.text: In 2019, as a councilwoman, she voted against all four cannabis business approvals in the city, citing concerns about concentration near schools and low-income neighborhoods. In 2026, she urged residents to ask the City Council to adopt a moratorium on new data center applications, saying the city needed time to evaluate the industry’s impacts. According to her campaign questionnaire, her administration has delivered affordable housing, transitional housing for homeless residents, veterans’ housing, senior housing, and market-rate homes. She states that balancing rising costs and pension liabilities requires fiscal discipline. She opposed a 2026 proposal to eliminate the elected mayor position, stating the role provides independent oversight and that she was targeted for questioning police contracts. On the council, she supported measures to protect youth from tobacco and vaping products, and advocated for a joint-use agreement with the school district to open more greenspace.
